rows.grounds: absolutive of paṭh 'to recite'; indicates prior completed action
refers to the preceding formula or instruction
compound śava+pṛṣṭha; locus of the prescribed practice
describes the practitioner's concentrated mental state

items.question: What recitation and mental state are required while positioned upon the corpse's back?
premises: The practitioner has recited the preceding formula thus.
The great goddess is directly addressed in this act.
The practitioner is positioned upon the corpse's back.
The practitioner maintains a composed mental state.
items.inference: Proper performance requires reciting the formula thus while remaining composed upon the corpse's back.
uncertainties: Whether śavapṛṣṭhaṃ implies literal placement on a corpse or a symbolic locus is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Having thus recited, O great goddess, one remains composed upon the corpse's back.
